Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 11046 - 1984 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
TOWEL, OPERATING 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 15 March 1984, after the draft finalized by the Made-up Textile 
Items Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division 
Council. 

0.2 The towel covered in this standard is used in operation theatres by 
the medical staff. This standard is based on JSS 7210-8, issued by the 
Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, ex- 
pressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes constructional details and other particulars 
of towel, operating. 

2. MATERIAL 

2.1 The towel shall be made from the following materials, conforming to 
the particulars quoted against each: 

Components Materials Particulars 

a) Body /)oj«/tV230 g/m2 IS : 179-1977t or 

IS : 756-1955: 

b) Tape Tape, 13 mm, IS : 179-1977t 

Dosuti, 230 g/m2 IS : 756- 1955 J 

c) Sewings Sewings cotton, GOs/G IS : 1720-1978§ 

( lOOdtex X 6) 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised), 
tCotton dosiiti ( second revision ). 

{Handioom cotton dosuti grey, scoured, bleached or dyed. 
§Cotton sewing threads ( second revision ). 

2 



IS : 11046 - 1984 
3. MANUFACTURE 

3.1 Body — The towel shall be made from a single piece of dosuti. The 
two raw ends of the dosuti shall be hemmed as shown in Fig. 1. The 
selvedges shall not be hemmed. A 270 mm long piece of tape, 13 mm 
wide ( see 3.2 ), made from dosuti, shall be sewn at the centre of one of 
the hemmed sides to form a loop of about 100 mm as shown in Fig. L 

3.2 Tape — It shall be manufactured from two fold dosuli. Both the 
raw edges shall be turned 5 mm inside and stitched together with a single 
row of lock stitch by machine. The body and tape shall be of same 
material. 

' 3.3 Sewings — The towel shall be assembled throughout with lock- 
stitch regulated at 35 to 40 stitches per diameter. All stitches shall be 
securely fastened off. 

3.4 Colour — All the materials of towel may be opaline green or any 
other colour, as specified in contract or order. 

4. REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 The towel shall conform to the dimensions and other constructional 
particulars as shown in Fig. K 

4.2 Scaled Sample — If, in order to illustrate or specify the indetermi- 
nable characteristics, such as workmanship, general appearance, lustre, 
feel and shade of the cloth, a sample has been agreed upon and sealed, 
the supply shall be in conformity with the sample in such respects. 

4.2.1 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a matter of prior 
agreement between the buyer and the seller, 

5. MARKING 

5.1 Each towel, shall have a white cloth label of 50 X 40 mm securely 
sewn at one corner, on which the following shall be marked legibly with 
indelible ink ( see IS : 394-1963* ): 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark, if any; 

b) Year of manufacture; 

c) Size; and 

d) Any other information required by the buyer. 



♦Specification for ink, cloth marking ( nviied).

S.l.l The towels may alvSO be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regu- 
lations made thereunder. 7 he ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produce d to comply with the require- 
ments of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the protlucer. ISI 
marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the 
use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, 
may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 

6. PACKING 

6.1 The operating towels shall be packed as specified in the contract or 
order. 

7. SAMPLING 

7.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and the seller, 
procedure given in IS : 2500 ( Part 1 )-1973* shall be followed for 
sampling inspection. 

7.2 For dimensional and other constructional particulars, the single 
sampling plan witii inspection level III and AQL 2*5 percent in Table 1 
and 2 of IS : 2500 ( Part 1 )-1973* shall be followed. 



♦Sampling inspection tables: Part 1 Inspection by attributes and by count of 
defects.
